tools.name: Cursor
tools.what: AI-first code editor built on VS Code.
tools.verdict: The default pick if you want agentic edits inside a familiar editor.

tools.name: Windsurf
tools.what: AI code editor with an agent mode.
tools.verdict: Solid Cursor alternative; try both and keep the one that fits your flow.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.what: GitHub's AI pair programmer for many editors.
tools.verdict: Safest choice if your team already lives on GitHub.

tools.name: Zed
tools.what: Fast, open-source code editor with AI features.
tools.verdict: Pick it for speed; AI is a bonus, not the headline.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.what: Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal.
tools.verdict: Strong for repo-wide changes when you're comfortable in a shell.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.what: OpenAI's coding agent for terminal, IDE and cloud.
tools.verdict: Worth it if you're already paying for ChatGPT.

tools.name: Aider
tools.what: Open-source AI pair programming in your terminal.
tools.verdict: Best free, bring-your-own-key terminal option.

tools.name: Warp
tools.what: Modern terminal with built-in AI agents.
tools.verdict: Nice upgrade if your terminal still feels like 1995.

tools.name: Replit
tools.what: Browser IDE with an agent that builds and hosts apps.
tools.verdict: Fastest path from idea to hosted app with zero setup.

tools.name: Bolt
tools.what: Prompt-to-full-stack web app in the browser.
tools.verdict: Great for quick prototypes; export before it gets big.

tools.name: Lovable
tools.what: Builds web apps from chat prompts.
tools.verdict: Friendliest for non-coders shipping a first product.

tools.name: v0
tools.what: Vercel's generator for UI and full apps.
tools.verdict: Best for clean React/Next.js UI you'll keep editing.

tools.name: LangGraph
tools.what: Framework for stateful, multi-step agent graphs.
tools.verdict: Use when you need control over every agent step.

tools.name: CrewAI
tools.what: Framework for role-based multi-agent crews.
tools.verdict: Easiest way to try multi-agent teams in Python.

tools.name: AutoGen
tools.what: Microsoft's open-source multi-agent framework.
tools.verdict: Good for research-style multi-agent experiments.

tools.name: Model Context Protocol
tools.what: Open standard for connecting AI apps to tools and data.
tools.verdict: Learn it: it's how agents plug into everything now.

tools.name: n8n
tools.what: Workflow automation with AI nodes; self-hostable.
tools.verdict: Best value automation if you can self-host.

tools.name: Zapier Agents
tools.what: AI agents that act across Zapier's app integrations.
tools.verdict: Pick it for breadth of integrations, not price.

tools.name: Make
tools.what: Visual automation builder with AI modules.
tools.verdict: Great visual middle ground between Zapier and n8n.

tools.name: Browserbase
tools.what: Headless browser infrastructure for AI agents.
tools.verdict: Use when your agent needs real browsers at scale.

tools.name: Firecrawl
tools.what: Turns websites into LLM-ready data.
tools.verdict: Quickest way to feed web pages to an agent.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.what: Open-source browser automation and testing.
tools.verdict: Free, reliable foundation for any browser agent.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.what: Run open models locally.
tools.verdict: Easiest way to run models on your own machine.

tools.name: LM Studio
tools.what: Desktop app to download and run local models.
tools.verdict: Best GUI for local models; no terminal needed.

tools.name: Hugging Face
tools.what: Hub for open models, datasets and demos.
tools.verdict: The library of open AI; bookmark it.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.what: One API for many model providers.
tools.verdict: Use it to swap models without rewriting code.

tools.name: Groq
tools.what: Fast inference for open models.
tools.verdict: Pick it when latency matters more than anything.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.what: OpenAI's general AI assistant.
tools.verdict: The all-rounder most people start with.

tools.name: Claude
tools.what: Anthropic's AI assistant.
tools.verdict: Excellent for long documents and careful writing.

tools.name: Gemini
tools.what: Google's AI assistant.
tools.verdict: Best if you live in Google Workspace.

tools.name: Grok
tools.what: xAI's AI assistant, connected to X.
tools.verdict: Best for real-time takes on what X is talking about.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.what: AI answer engine with cited sources.
tools.verdict: Go-to for quick research with sources attached.

tools.name: NotebookLM
tools.what: Google's research notebook grounded in your sources.
tools.verdict: Best free tool for studying your own docs.

tools.name: DeepL
tools.what: AI translation and writing assistant.
tools.verdict: Our pick for EN/NO/DE/NL/ES/PT translation quality.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.what: AI voice, dubbing and text-to-speech.
tools.verdict: Top pick for multilingual voiceovers and dubbing.

tools.name: Descript
tools.what: Edit video and audio by editing text.
tools.verdict: Fastest way to cut podcasts and talking-head video.

tools.name: Suno
tools.what: AI music generation from prompts.
tools.verdict: Most fun tool on this list; great for soundtracks.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.what: AI image generation.
tools.verdict: Still the taste leader for striking images.

tools.name: Runway
tools.what: AI video generation and editing.
tools.verdict: Go-to for AI video experiments.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.what: AI image generation strong at text in images.
tools.verdict: Pick it when your image needs readable text.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.what: Postgres backend with auth and storage.
tools.verdict: Default backend for vibe-coded apps.

tools.name: Vercel
tools.what: Frontend cloud for hosting web apps.
tools.verdict: Smoothest deploys for Next.js projects.

tools.name: Netlify
tools.what: Hosting and deploys for static and web apps.
tools.verdict: Great free hosting for static sites (this one runs on it).

tools.name: Resend
tools.what: Email API for developers.
tools.verdict: Cleanest way for an app or agent to send email.

tools.name: PostHog
tools.what: Product analytics, session replay and flags.
tools.verdict: Generous free tier; one tool instead of five.

tools.name: Sentry
tools.what: Error and performance monitoring.
tools.verdict: Install it before your users find the bugs.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.what: Open-source LLM observability and evals.
tools.verdict: Use it to see what your agent actually did.

tools.name: CodeRabbit
tools.what: AI code review on pull requests.
tools.verdict: Cheap second reviewer for solo builders.

new_releases.note: Persistent browser tool: tabs and logins last between agent turns (SDK v0.28.0+).

new_releases.name: Meta Muse Wonder
new_releases.note: New Meta coding/agent model on Muse Code and Meta Model API.
